1. **[note] `Server/DevPublish.mjs:48`** — A merge into a tree with staged changes may sweep them into the merge commit. The overlap check at `:44-47` blocks only files that the incoming branch also changed. `git merge` builds its commit from the index, so an unrelated staged file could end up in the merge commit. I could not test this, because the git-guard hook blocks `git merge` in this tree. Fix: refuse the merge when `git diff --cached --quiet` is non-zero, or build the commit through a temp index the way `commitLanded` does. The fast-forward at `:39` is safe, since git refuses if an overlapping file is dirty.

2. **[fix] `Server/rename-dev-branch.mjs:104-107`** — The delete of the old remote branch relies on a possibly stale local `origin/michael/dev`. Nothing fetches after `plan()`, so the `inside` ancestor check can pass against old data. Another clone or a cloud agent may have pushed to `michael/dev` meanwhile, and `git push origin --delete` would then destroy those commits. A PR whose head is that branch also closes on delete. Fix: `git fetch origin` before the check, or use `git push --force-with-lease`-style deletion.

3. **[note] `Server/rename-dev-branch.mjs:83-95`** — The script rewrites files before it runs `git branch -m`, and there is no rollback. If `branch -m` fails, 80 or more files stay edited in the shared tree and uncommitted. Fix: run `branch -m` first, or restore from `git stash`/`git checkout` on failure.

4. **[note] `Server/rename-dev-branch.mjs:17-18,36`** — Classification risks. The `HISTORY_NAMES` rule treats any `review.md`, `report.md` or `requirements.md` as history, so a live doc such as `Server/doc/review.md` keeps the old name. `public/framework/ai/rail/overview/overview.json` (10 mentions) and `todo.md` / `handover.md` (mixed live and history) are rewritten. Code that matches old `.jsonl` records on the literal name, for example `Servex/Landed.js` and `Pool.js`, will stop matching those records, because the history is left alone.

5. **[note] `Server/rename-dev-branch.mjs:79,109`** — Lock handling is correct. It uses `wx`, unlinks in `finally`, and a stale lock refuses cleanly. Only the preconditions check at `:77` is loose: any problem other than "origin/… does not exist" blocks the apply, which is the safe direction.

**Q3 — publish to main.** It is off by default: `publish.json` is `{"main":false}` and `publish_on` returns false on a parse error. It also needs `push_dev` to succeed. There is no force-push: the pushes at `:63,:67,:131` are plain, and the merge goes through the PR API with `merge_method: "merge"`. The local `main` update is `fetch origin main:main`, which git refuses unless it is a fast-forward. Only one thing is odd. A set `MERGE_PUBLISH_MAIN` that is not exactly `"1"`, such as `true`, forces it off, which is the safe direction.

**Q2 — what the rename never touches.** `main` and `production` are never touched. The remote delete is skipped when `origin/michael/dev` is missing.
